name: PSP or acquirer product lead
oneLine: Tokens, routing, risk, fees, and support for many protocols at once.
goals: Offer merchants one integration that accepts agent orders from ACP, UCP, TAP and MPP.
Issue and vault scoped payment tokens (SPTs, vault tokens, network agentic tokens) with usage limits.
Route agent transactions through the right network token (VIC or Agent Pay) and pass agent indicators in the authorization message.
Keep fraud and dispute rates flat as agent volume grows.
Price agent transactions without new interchange surprises.
Host Delegate Payment and similar endpoints so merchants never touch raw card data.
pains: The protocol count keeps growing and each one has dated versions, so the integration surface is never finished.
Agent indicators are not reliably present in authorization messages, so issuers cannot distinguish agent traffic and decline rates are unpredictable.
SPTs and vault tokens are products, not standards, and competitors run their own, so merchants ask for all of them.

Visa calls none of its agent rules a liability shift (Worldpay: none exists yet), so acquirers and merchants still face disputes about what an agent bought. Issuers must pay for Agentic Transactions made under cardholder instructions, and from 2026-10-24 a provider's login ID counts among the evidence that can defeat a card-absent fraud dispute.
Stablecoin rails (x402, MPP on Tempo) settle small payments on chain with no card acquirer in the flow.
Idempotency and replay rules differ by protocol (Idempotency-Key, challenge id, nonce), and bugs here create duplicate charges.
decisions: Which protocols to support in the agentic commerce product and which to leave to partners.
Token scope defaults: amount, currency, expiry, single-use or reusable.
Risk thresholds for agent-initiated transactions and when to require 3DS2.
Whether to run an x402 or MPP facilitator alongside card processing.
How to report agent orders to merchants and issuers.
